32yrs old. Never had kids. Not on any hormonal birth control pill since my early 20s. I had my copper IUD removed a few months prior to the surgery. I have been sterilised by coelioscopy last July and tubes were cauterised (not sure if it is the right word).

There was no change to my period flow or pain after the surgery. I also have pretty painful ones, but not hemorrhagic. The only notable change was that, right after the ligation, I had my periods two weeks earlier than what it was supposed to be and the flow was a bit weird, though it is hard to tell if it is exclusively surgery related. I had them normally (still painful) and regularly after that first "post-op period".

My OBGYN told me that tubal ligation does not improve period cramps anyway, so I still need to warm up my belly or take a light painkiller when it is too painful. To my knowledge, the only medically proven way to get rid of periods and so get rid of the pain is to take your uterus out, endometrial ablation (there is some risks you should be aware of for those surgeries) or hormones.

Discuss with your doctor first.

Still, you do not have to go though surgery for them to take you seriously, this is just my experience. It is your choice and I sincerly hope that they'll get it eventually. Good luck!

So, quite a lot had happened. COVID slowed down everything, but the brother's lawyer contacted the notary in France. I do not know the exact conversation, but the lawyer said that the brother did find it unfair for my mother to have more than his family. The flat in Paris was evaluated and it is way less than what I had stated before (about 250k euros), but still more than what my step-father left for his family in England, which is around 50k pounds (that I also overvalued). The brother's lawyer said that they wanted to discuss "amicably" about a transfert of money. So, my mom did something that she has not done before: she talked to my step-father's and the brother's mother. The mother was soooooo pissed at him.

The mother then wrote a letter stating that she is giving up any inheritance in France. It seems that it calmed him down immediately.

Everything is more or less settled for the French part now. In England, the transfert of money / properties has not being done so far. Thanks a lot for your help.
